result.title: Can Agents Truly Forget? Explore Machine Unlearning for LLM Agents
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown strong capabilities in interactive problem solving, tool use, and long-horizon task execution. However, they may also acquire sensitive or private knowledge during training and expose it during deployment. Retraining a model from scratch to remove such knowledge is prohibitively costly, making machine unlearning a more practical approach. Machine unlearning aims to remove targeted undesirable knowledge from trained models without retraining from scratch while preserving general utility. When language models are deployed as agents, parameter-level unlearning becomes insufficient: forgotten information may still persist in memory artifacts or be reacquired via tool calls. In this paper, we formulate the problem of agent unlearning as removing private information from an LLM-based agent across three information channels: parametric knowledge, persistent memory, and tool-call acquisition. To study this problem, we introduce we introduce Agent Unlearning Benchmark (AUBench), a controlled benchmark that extends the fictitious-author setting of TOFU into an agent environment with persistent memory, an offline web snapshot, tool-accessible documents, and provenance-tracked interaction trajectories. By evaluating existing parameter-level and memory-level unlearning methods in this setting, AUBench reveals the gap between model-level forgetting and system-level agent unlearning, and provides a foundation for developing unlearning methods that operate across the full lifecycle of LLM agents.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「agent 遗忘」形式化为需从参数知识、持久记忆与工具调用获取三条信息通道中移除私有信息的问题，并构建带持久记忆、离线网页快照与来源追踪轨迹的 AUBench 基准，用其评测现有参数级与记忆级遗忘方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「被遗忘的信息仍可能残留在记忆工件或经工具调用重新获得」的多通道观察与来源追踪轨迹设计，可能与 LVR 中判断答案是否真正使用 latent 内容、而非经旁路泄漏这一核心问题存在概念联系，可供核查其评测思路能否迁移到视觉证据筛选与贡献分配的场景。
